Tailor Toyo Men's 1950s Style Reversible Sukajan Souvenir Jacket, Cotton Velveteen and Quilted Acetate Satin, Insulated, Polar Bear and Alaska Map Embroidery (TT15974-145, Green)

Tailor Toyo

This men's reversible embroidered Japanese souvenir jacket, commonly known as a sukajan, is made in China and produced by Tailor Toyo, a Toyo Enterprises brand. The brand specializes in reproductions of vintage souvenir jackets as well as clothing and accessories inspired by the souvenir jacket style. Based on a late-1950s jacket originally made by Kosho & Co., Toyo Enterprises' predecessor, for sale at U.S. military base exchanges in Alaska, this model recreates the distinctive combination of polar bears, dog sleds, and an Alaska map associated with the style known as the Alaska souvenir jacket. Deep green 100% cotton velveteen on one side is paired with black and ivory 100% acetate satin on the reverse, with cotton-and-polyester batting between the two faces and diamond quilting on the satin side. Rayon embroidery, raglan sleeves, double-layer rib-knit trim, slanted double-welt pockets, and a metal zipper with pulls on both faces complete the reversible construction. A regular fit with moderate room through the torso, a short body length, and a rib-knit waistband gives the jacket its rounded, classic silhouette, carrying the materials and detailing of the original design into contemporary casual wear.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

The sizing of this jacket is generally closer to Japanese men's sizing than to standard U.S./EU sizing. As a result, the tagged size may fit somewhat smaller than the same letter size from many U.S. or European brands. As an approximate reference, a tagged size M would generally correspond to a U.S./EU men's size S, approximately a U.S. 36 or EU 46. This conversion is intended only as a general guide, since the appropriate size will also depend on body proportions, preferred fit, and the thickness of the clothing worn underneath.

The silhouette follows the classic proportions of a late-1950s souvenir jacket, combining a regular fit with moderate room around the torso and a relatively short body length. The stretchy rib-knit waistband sits gently around the waist and draws in the lower edge of the body. Together with the thickness of the batting, this creates a naturally rounded shape through the body when worn.

Raglan sleeves run diagonally from near the neckline to the underarms, creating a continuous line from the shoulder area into the upper arm without a conventional shoulder-to-sleeve seam at the shoulder tip. Stretchy rib-knit cuffs allow the sleeve openings to sit naturally around the wrists.

The jacket contains insulating batting, held in place by diamond quilting on the satin side. Because this padding adds thickness, the jacket may feel different from an unpadded, lightweight souvenir jacket with the same flat chest-width measurement. The thickness of your layers, your body proportions, and your preferred amount of room will also affect the fit. For the most useful comparison, please measure a similar jacket that fits you well, preferably one with comparable padding and construction, and compare its width, body length, and center-back sleeve length with the measurements below.

Model and Reversible Color Arrangement

Tailor Toyo and the Japanese Souvenir Jacket Tradition
Tailor Toyo is Toyo Enterprises' souvenir-jacket label, continuing the history and design tradition inherited from Kosho & Co., the company's predecessor. The Japanese souvenir jacket, commonly called a sukajan, developed after World War II as American servicemen stationed in Japan had jackets embroidered as mementos of their time overseas. Designs included eagles, tigers, dragons, Mount Fuji, cherry blossoms, place names, and military unit names.

Kosho & Co. was involved in producing and supplying souvenir jackets from the early postwar years and played a significant role in the development of this clothing tradition. Tailor Toyo carries that history forward through reproductions that retain the materials, construction details, and embroidered imagery associated with period garments.

Late-1950s Alaska Souvenir Jacket Design
This model draws on a vintage souvenir jacket made by Kosho & Co. at the request of the U.S. military in the late 1950s and sold at PX stores, or military base exchanges, in Alaska. Its combination of polar bears against lightning motifs, dog-sled embroidery running along the sleeves, and an Alaska map on the reverse recreates the regional imagery associated with the style often called the Alaska souvenir jacket.

The reversible construction combines a pile-surfaced velveteen face with a quilted satin face, with insulating batting between them. Each side is designed to be worn outward, presenting a different fabric texture, color arrangement, and embroidery composition within the same jacket.

100% Cotton Velveteen with a Short, Dense Pile
The velveteen side uses deep green 100% cotton fabric throughout the body and sleeves. Velveteen is a woven pile fabric with short fibers closely covering its surface. This dense, short pile gives the cloth a soft surface appearance and a subdued sheen.

The pile reflects light differently depending on its direction and the angle of illumination. As a result, areas of the same green fabric can appear lighter or darker, creating tonal depth across the curved body panels and along the moving sleeves. These changes in shading are part of the appearance of the piled surface.

The lustrous rayon embroidery contrasts with the softer sheen of the velveteen. Individual stitches and overlapping threads add raised texture above the short pile, giving the embroidered motifs a dimensional appearance against the green ground.

100% Acetate Satin Reverse with Contrasting Body and Sleeves
The reverse is made from 100% acetate satin, combining a black body with ivory sleeves. The different colors make the diagonal raglan sleeve junctions clearly visible and give this side a different appearance from the uniformly green velveteen face.

The satin has a smooth surface and a reflective sheen that changes with the viewing angle, folds in the fabric, and the direction of the light. Its smooth, lustrous appearance contrasts with the short pile of the velveteen, allowing the reversible design to present two distinct fabric surfaces.

Cotton-Polyester Batting and Diamond Quilting
The insulating batting is composed of 80% cotton and 20% polyester. Positioned between the velveteen and satin faces, it adds thickness and contributes to the rounded body shape of the finished jacket.

On the satin side, intersecting diagonal rows of stitching form a diamond quilting pattern. These stitches secure the batting to the satin and help limit movement and uneven distribution of the fill inside the jacket.

The quilting lines sit slightly below the surrounding satin surface, while the batting gives the areas between the stitches a gently raised profile. The diamond stitching also crosses the embroidered sections, bringing the quilting lines and the individual embroidery stitches together on the same surface.

Reversible Metal Front Zipper with Pulls on Both Faces
The front closes with a metal zipper. The slider has a pull on each face, allowing the zipper to be operated with either the velveteen side or the satin side facing outward.

The rectangular metal pull tabs are stamped with "T.Y.E." and "TOKYO." Their shape and markings form part of the period-style hardware detailing used throughout this reproduction.

Raglan Sleeves with Lengthwise Contrast Panels on the Satin Side
The sleeves are joined to the body with diagonal seams running from near the neckline down toward the underarms. There is no conventional sleeve attachment seam at the shoulder tip, allowing the outline to continue gradually from the shoulder area into the upper arm.

On the satin side, the ivory sleeves incorporate black fabric panels running along their length. These contrasting sections add a lengthwise detail to the sleeves, while the black body and ivory sleeve areas emphasize the diagonal raglan construction.

Double-Layer Acrylic Rib-Knit Collar, Cuffs, and Waistband
The collar, cuffs, and waistband are made from 100% acrylic rib knit. Each rib-knit section is folded back on itself to create a double layer and then attached to the jacket, providing flexible, stretchy finishes at the neck, wrists, and lower body.

The rib-knit collar follows the curve of the neckline, with its two front ends meeting the upper portion of the zipper. Its curved shape forms a continuous knitted finish around the neck opening.

The waistband stretches to sit gently around the waist and draws in the bottom of the body. This gathered lower edge works with the short body length and the thickness of the batting to give the jacket its characteristic rounded silhouette.

The sleeve ends are finished with tubular rib-knit cuffs. Their knitted structure allows them to stretch around the wrists and hold the sleeve openings in a naturally close-fitting shape.

Slanted Double-Welt Hand Pockets on Both Sides
Both wearable faces have a hand pocket at each side of the waist. Each opening is set at a slant for hand access and finished with two narrow welts, one bordering each side of the opening.

On the velveteen face, the welts use the same green velveteen as the body, blending the pocket edges into the surrounding color and pile texture. On the satin face, the welts contrast with the body color, making the outlines of the pocket openings more visible.

The satin-side pocket openings have triangular reinforcement stitching at both ends. These stitched areas reinforce the points that receive repeated stress as hands are placed into and removed from the pockets.

Brand and Size Labels Inside the Left Velveteen-Side Pocket
The Tailor Toyo woven brand label and size tag are attached inside the left pocket on the velveteen side. Locating these labels within the pocket keeps them off the visible body surface regardless of which side of the jacket is worn outward.

100% Rayon Embroidery with Directional Stitching
The embroidery is worked in 100% rayon thread. Its luster reflects light differently from the velveteen and satin grounds, helping define the motifs against each fabric surface.

The direction of the stitches changes across different parts of the designs. As light reaches these differently oriented threads, it creates variations in brightness and shadow. The combination of directional stitching and overlapping threads gives the embroidery depth and texture.

Polar Bear and Dog-Sled Embroidery on Green Velveteen
The velveteen side features polar bears with lightning motifs on the chest and back, together with dog-sled embroidery extending along both sleeves. The placement carries the Alaska-themed imagery across the front, back, and length of the arms.

Surviving period souvenir jackets made from green velveteen are uncommon. This reproduction recreates the distinctive combination of that historical green colorway and the Alaska-themed embroidered designs.

Alaska Map Embroidery on the Satin Reverse
The back of the satin side features an embroidered map of Alaska. Place names are accompanied by imagery including Dall sheep, an igloo, and Mount McKinley, combining regional animals, structures, and scenery within the map design. The diamond quilting passes through the embroidered area, allowing the map imagery and quilted surface texture to remain visible together.

Made in China
This Tailor Toyo jacket is made in China. Its cotton velveteen and acetate satin faces offer different textures and color arrangements, while the Alaska-themed rayon embroidery gives each side its own visual character.

Insulating batting, diamond quilting, reversible zipper hardware, double-welt pockets, and rib-knit trim bring together the construction details associated with the original souvenir-jacket style. The result preserves the design tradition inherited from Kosho & Co. and the distinctive character of the late-1950s Alaska jacket in a newly made reproduction for everyday casual wear.

Tailor Toyo by Toyo Enterprises, Lot No. TT15974-145 / Late 1950s Style Velveteen Souvenir Jacket "POLAR BEAR" × "ALASKA MAP".

Sukajan History

- The "sukajan" (Japanese souvenir jacket) is a unique piece of postwar history that blends American and Japanese culture. The name is widely believed to come from the phrase "Yokosuka jumper," referring to the Yokosuka area near a U.S. Navy base in Japan, where these jackets became widely known. After World War II, many American servicemen stationed in Japan ordered custom jackets as memorable keepsakes to bring home. Japanese makers embroidered these jackets with bold, detailed designs, often featuring motifs such as eagles, dragons, cherry blossoms, Mt. Fuji, and tigers. The result was a distinctive mix of American military imagery and traditional Japanese artwork.

- In the early years, embroidery was sometimes added to existing military or bomber-style jackets. Over time, souvenir jackets were increasingly made using glossy satin fabrics, especially acetate and rayon satin, and sometimes silk, as well as cotton velveteen, which gave them an eye-catching look and made the embroidery stand out even more.

- Sukajan later gained popularity in Japan as well, especially from the 1960s through the 1970s, becoming closely associated with youth fashion and rebellious subcultures. Depending on the era and the wearer, the jacket carried layered meaning: a reminder of postwar memories and American influence for some, and a symbol of individuality and nonconformity for others.

- Today, sukajan continues to be appreciated worldwide as wearable art, valued for its craftsmanship, cultural significance, and bold embroidered storytelling.

- Tailor Toyo (a label under Toyo Enterprises) is deeply connected to this history. The company, originally known as KOSHO & CO., supplied souvenir jackets to PX (Post Exchange) stores on U.S. military bases and has preserved sukajan-making tradition since the 1940s. In 1965, Toyo Enterprises was formally established, carrying that legacy forward under the Tailor Toyo name.

Care Instructions
Do not wash at home, either by hand or machine.
Do not bleach.
Do not tumble dry.
Do not iron.
Professional dry cleaning with petroleum-based solvents is permitted using a mild process.
Do not wet clean.
Please consult a professional cleaner before cleaning this garment.

This is a delicate garment that reproduces the fabric textures, color combinations, stitching, embroidery, and zipper details of vintage souvenir jackets. The appearance of the velveteen changes with the direction of its pile, and rubbing or pressure may flatten the fibers or leave visible marks. Avoid strong friction or prolonged pressure on the same area during wear and storage.

The acetate satin may develop surface abrasion or pulled threads if rubbed or snagged. Take care around bags, accessories, hook-and-loop fasteners, and sharp objects. Prolonged exposure to sunlight or artificial lighting, as well as storage conditions, may cause fading or discoloration.

Fine puckering, wrinkles, or unevenness may appear around the embroidery and quilting where the stitching draws on the fabric. Individual garments may also vary in the appearance of embroidery stitches, outlines, overlapping threads, and thread ends. Do not pull hard on or cut protruding embroidery or quilting threads.

Always follow the care instructions attached to the actual product. Because the jacket combines cotton velveteen, acetate satin, rayon embroidery, cotton-and-polyester batting, and acrylic rib knit, avoid rubbing or pulling forcefully on any one area.

Important Notes
- Our inventory is shared among our physical retail store and multiple online stores, so inventory changes may not always be reflected immediately on each website.
- Even after an order has been placed, an item may occasionally be sold out due to the timing of simultaneous purchases. We sincerely appreciate your understanding.
- All measurements are taken manually with the garment laid flat.
- Because individual garments and measuring methods may vary, slight measurement differences may occur.
- The actual color of the product may appear slightly different from the photographs depending on lighting conditions and the settings of your monitor or display.

product.title: Sugar Cane Men's Vintage-Inspired 10.5 oz. Cotton and Sugarcane Fiber Denim Work Coat, Unlined Chore Jacket, Made in Japan (SC15920, 421A Indigo, One-Wash)
product.body_html:
Sugar Cane Men's Vintage-Inspired 10.5 oz. Cotton and Sugarcane Fiber Denim Work Coat, Unlined Chore Jacket, Made in Japan (SC15920, 421A Indigo, One-Wash)

Sugar Cane

This men's denim work coat is made in Japan by Sugar Cane, a Toyo Enterprises brand specializing in vintage-inspired American workwear. Based on work coats from the early 20th century, it is constructed from 10.5 oz. indigo denim woven from a blend of 85% cotton and 15% sugarcane fiber. The unlined construction combines five removable metal front buttons, a turn-down collar without a separate collar stand, two-piece set-in sleeves with reinforced adjustable openings, five practical pockets, and a two-panel back with a center seam. A slanted left chest utility pocket with a dedicated pen holder and visible stitching around the interior pocket give the coat the functional character of early work clothing. The one-wash finish softens the fabric's initial crispness while preserving its body, subtle slubs, and pale neps. The classic regular fit provides moderate room through the chest, while the body length falls around the hips. Together, these proportions create a comfortable, practical silhouette that makes this vintage-inspired work coat suitable for everyday casual wear.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

The coat has a classic regular fit with moderate room through the chest and a body length designed to cover the hip area. It is balanced between a close, slim cut and an oversized silhouette. The body falls relatively straight from the underarms toward the hem, without pronounced shaping at the waist. Its longer chore-coat proportions extend below the waist, giving it the outline of a traditional work coat rather than a cropped denim jacket.

The set-in sleeves are sewn into the body's armholes, creating defined shoulder seams. At the lower front, the edges curve gently from the bottom of the button opening into the hem, giving the front outline a softly rounded shape.

The construction reflects the practical need for ease of movement in workwear. Although the woven denim does not stretch, it gradually softens and conforms through wear and washing. Its surface color and the appearance around the stitched areas also develop over time, adding to the denim's individual character.

The fit will vary with your body type, the thickness of the layers worn underneath, and your preferred amount of room. To help you choose a size, please measure a similar work jacket or chore coat that fits you well and compare its chest width, body length, center-back sleeve length, shoulder-to-sleeve-end length, and shoulder width with the measurements below. Please allow room for your intended layers, as this is a non-stretch woven fabric.

Early-20th-Century Work Coat Design and Unlined Construction
The design draws on the practical construction of American work coats from the early 20th century. Its button front, varied pocket arrangement, and hip-covering length retain the character of that workwear tradition, while the regular fit makes the coat suitable for contemporary casual wear.

The coat is unlined, allowing the relatively lightweight 10.5 oz. denim to form the main structure without an additional lining layer. It can be worn as a light outer layer from spring into early fall, with further opportunities for wear throughout the year depending on the weather and the layers worn with it.

10.5 oz. Denim with 85% Cotton and 15% Sugarcane Fiber
The fabric is a non-stretch indigo denim woven from a blend of 85% cotton and 15% sugarcane fiber. It weighs 10.5 oz. and uses No. 9 yarns for the lengthwise warp and No. 11 yarns for the crosswise weft.

The warp yarns are indigo-dyed, while the weft yarns retain their natural, undyed ecru color. Small glimpses of these lighter weft yarns appear between the indigo warp yarns, creating fine tonal variation across the face of the fabric. This interaction gives the denim a subtly mottled, almost heathered appearance while maintaining its overall indigo character.

The depth of color comes from the relationship between the darker and lighter yarns within the woven structure. The result is a restrained indigo tone with visible variation rather than a uniformly flat surface.

Slubbed Texture, Pale Neps, and a Supple Yet Structured Hand
Subtle variations in yarn thickness create small slubs across the surface, accompanied by scattered pale neps, fine surface fibers, and irregular shifts in tone. Together, these features give the cloth a textured appearance associated with vintage workwear.

The pale neps add a lightly flecked effect to the indigo ground. Their appearance combines with the visible ecru weft and uneven yarn texture to produce a rustic, workwear-oriented character.

At 10.5 oz., the denim is relatively lightweight while retaining moderate crispness and body. It also has enough suppleness to bend and settle during wear. This balance gives the coat a defined shape without the heavier feel of a more substantial denim outer layer.

One-Wash Finish and Gradual Indigo Aging
The coat is washed once as part of the finishing process. This initial wash softens some of the fabric's crispness while leaving enough body to support the work-coat shape, giving the garment a more settled feel from the first wear.

Compared with an unwashed garment, the one-wash finish reduces the likelihood of substantial initial shrinkage. It does not rule out further dimensional changes: some additional shrinkage or variation may occur depending on subsequent washing and drying conditions and differences between individual garments.

With repeated wear and washing, the fabric gradually becomes more familiar to the wearer, while the indigo develops natural fading and tonal contrast. Changes in the fabric surface and around the stitched areas contribute to the coat's evolving denim character.

Five-Button Front with Folded Denim Facings
The front closes with five buttons, including the top button at the neckline. From the wearer's perspective, the buttons sit on the right front edge, with corresponding horizontal buttonholes on the left. The lower front edges curve gently into the hem, creating the rounded outline of the coat's front opening.

The denim is turned inward along the opening and secured with stitching to form a double-layer front edge. These folded facings continue up to the neckline. The stitching that secures their edges follows a gently curved path from the upper front toward the lower hem, making the facing construction visible from the outside.

The overlapping layers reinforce the fabric around the buttons and buttonholes, where repeated opening and closing place stress on the cloth. They also help the front opening retain its shape and limit stretching or distortion along the edges.

Removable Antique-Finish Metal Change Buttons
The five front buttons are metal buttons with an antiqued finish. Each uses a removable change-button attachment: a loop-shaped metal shank on the back of the button passes through an attachment hole in the front edge and is secured from the inside with a metal retaining ring.

Removing the retaining ring releases the button, allowing it to be detached or replaced without cutting and resewing an attachment thread. The buttons can also be removed for laundering to reduce strain on the hardware and surrounding fabric.

This construction reproduces a practical fastening system found on vintage workwear that required frequent washing and repair. Its function is reflected in the separate button, shank, and retaining-ring components, while the aged metal finish contributes to the coat's period-inspired appearance.

Turn-Down Collar without a Separate Collar Stand
The collar is sewn directly to the body's neckline without a separate collar stand. This allows it to turn back relatively flat around the neck instead of rising on a distinct standing band.

When all five front buttons are fastened, the front closes up to the neckline and reduces the opening at the throat. Leaving only the top button undone and turning the upper front edges outward creates a V-shaped opening. The collar points and folded front edges then form an outline that resembles notched lapels.

The facings extend up to the neckline, supporting this change in how the front is worn. Adjusting the top button and the way the front edges are turned back changes the appearance around the collar.

Two-Piece Set-In Sleeves
Each sleeve is assembled from two fabric panels and sewn into the corresponding armhole in the body. This set-in construction creates a defined seam where the sleeve meets the shoulder and body, while the seam joining the two sleeve panels forms part of the coat's visible construction.

Two-Position Sleeve Openings with Reinforced Slits
A slit extends upward from each sleeve end, allowing the fabric to overlap and close with a button. One side has a single horizontal buttonhole, while the opposite side carries two metal buttons at different fastening positions. Choosing between the two buttons changes the amount of overlap and provides two settings for the fit around the wrist.

When unbuttoned, the slit opens more widely so the hand can pass through more easily when putting on or removing the coat. The sleeve-end edge and the edges of the slit are turned inward and secured with stitching, creating a folded finish around the opening.

Gently curved stitch lines extend from near the top of the slit toward both sides of the sleeve opening. Near the upper end of the slit, multiple lengthwise stitch lines and a horizontal bartack provide additional reinforcement. This supports the area subjected to repeated pulling as the opening is spread or the hand passes through, helping limit tearing from the top of the slit.

Fixed Metal Sleeve Buttons with Raised Brand Lettering
The sleeve buttons also have an antiqued metal finish, but their attachment differs from that of the removable front buttons. They are fixed to the fabric with metal tacks rather than held in place by removable retaining rings.

The button faces carry the brand logo in raised, decorative lettering. The relief of the lettering and the subdued metal tone add detail around the wrists while continuing the coat's classic workwear appearance.

Five-Pocket Layout and Open-Top Right Chest Pocket
The coat has five pockets in total: one on each side of the chest, one on each side of the lower front, and one inside the wearer's right front body panel.

The right chest pocket is an open-top patch pocket sewn onto the exterior of the coat. Its straightforward opening contrasts with the more specialized construction of the utility pocket on the opposite side.

Slanted Left Chest Utility Pocket with a Separate Pen Opening
The left chest pocket has a five-sided, home-plate-shaped outline and is attached at an angle. The portion of its upper edge nearest the front opening is stitched closed and does not serve as an entrance to the pocket. Excluding the dedicated pen opening, there is only one access opening, located along part of the slanted upper edge.

Stitching near the top partially divides the upper portion of the main storage area, but it does not separate the interior into fully independent compartments. The main pocket remains connected as a single storage space. This partial closure appears intended to help keep small items from falling out.

On the outer side of the pocket, toward the coat's side seam, an additional stitch line defines a narrow pen holder. This section has its own entrance for inserting a pen, keeping that dedicated opening distinct from the main storage opening.

Large Lower Patch Pockets with Bartack Reinforcement
Large open-top patch pockets are positioned on both sides of the lower front, providing accessible storage for everyday items. Their size and placement reflect the practical carrying needs associated with a work coat.

Bartacks reinforce the upper corners of each pocket. These concentrated rows of stitching strengthen the points where pulling forces are applied as items are inserted or removed, supporting the pocket openings during repeated use.

Interior Right Pocket with Externally Visible Attachment Stitching
An open-top interior pocket is sewn to the inside of the wearer's right front panel. Its attachment stitching passes through the body fabric and is visible on the exterior, forming an outline around the sides and lower edge of the external right chest pocket.

This visible stitching makes the relationship between the inner and outer pockets readable from the outside. It is a functional construction detail that also contributes to the layered arrangement of stitch lines on the front of the coat.

Two-Panel Back with a Center Seam
The back is made from separate left and right body panels joined along the center back. The resulting vertical seam defines the two-panel construction and adds a clear structural line to the rear of the coat.

Sewn-On Neck Patch with Visible Back Stitching
A cloth patch bearing the "SUGAR CANE & Co." design is sewn directly to the inside of the body at the back neck. Its attachment stitches also show on the outer upper back, where they form a rectangular outline.

This detail allows the way the interior patch is attached to remain visible as part of the coat's exterior stitchwork.

Vintage-Style Printed Labels inside the Pocket Opening
Printed cloth labels are sewn inside the opening of the interior pocket. Their designs recall the guarantee tickets and union labels found on vintage workwear.

Historically, labels of this kind served different purposes: some identified the manufacturer or stated a maker's quality guarantee, while union labels indicated that a garment had been produced by union members. Here, the period-inspired label designs extend the coat's classic workwear character to details on the inside.

Visible Stitching along the Garment's Construction Lines
Stitching follows the seams and joins throughout the coat, outlining the relationship between its fabric panels and components. Along with the visible interior-pocket and neck-patch stitching, these lines make the garment's construction an integral part of its appearance.

Made in Japan
Sugar Cane model SC15920 is made in Japan. Its cotton and sugarcane fiber denim, removable front buttons, adjustable sleeve openings, varied pocket structures, and visible stitchwork bring together the material and construction details of a vintage-inspired work coat.

The one-wash finish, unlined body, and regular proportions give these practical details a natural place in contemporary casual wear, while the indigo denim continues to develop through use.

Care Instructions
Machine wash on a gentle cycle at a maximum water temperature of 30°C (86°F).
Do not bleach.
Do not tumble dry.
Hang to dry in the shade.
Iron on a low setting with a pressing cloth.
Do not dry clean.

This garment is dyed with indigo. Color may fade through friction and laundering, and dye may transfer to other clothing. Please take particular care when the fabric is damp from perspiration or rain, as moisture can increase the likelihood of color transfer. During the early stages of wear, pairing the coat with dark-colored clothing is recommended. Wash the garment separately from other items.

The coat has been washed once during production. Some further shrinkage or other dimensional change may still occur depending on the washing and drying methods used and differences between individual garments.

Always follow the care instructions attached to the actual product.

product.title: TOYS McCOY Men's Vintage-Inspired Heavyweight Sweatpants, 100% Cotton Black Heather Brushed Fleece, Regular Straight Fit, Rib-Knit Waistband and Crotch Gusset, Waist and Hem Drawstrings, Unwashed, Made in Japan (TMC2665, 031 Black Heather)
product.body_html:
TOYS McCOY Men's Vintage-Inspired Heavyweight Sweatpants, 100% Cotton Black Heather Brushed Fleece, Regular Straight Fit, Rib-Knit Waistband and Crotch Gusset, Waist and Hem Drawstrings, Unwashed, Made in Japan (TMC2665, 031 Black Heather)

TOYS McCOY

These men's heavyweight sweatpants are made in Japan by TOYS McCOY. Drawing on the practical construction of classic American athletic wear and vintage sweatpants, this model brings together substantial cotton fabric, rib-knit inserts, reinforced drawstring openings, and adjustable details. The 100% cotton sweatshirt fleece has a black heather face with fine white yarns visible against the dark ground, while the brushed reverse provides a soft, warm interior. The legs are constructed without outside seams, and a stretchable rib-knit crotch gusset adds room and flexibility through the crotch. A rib-knit drawstring waistband, two vertical single-welt front pockets, a right rear patch pocket, and individual drawstrings at the open hems complete the design. The regular straight silhouette provides moderate room through the seat and thighs, with a gentle taper toward the hems. Left unwashed during production, the fabric retains its initial body and gradually changes with wear and careful washing. These vintage-inspired details combine in a practical pair of sweatpants for relaxed wear and everyday casual outfits.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

Fit: These sweatpants have a regular straight silhouette with moderate room through the seat and thighs and a slight taper from the knees to the leg openings. The proportions are balanced, without an excessively slim or oversized shape. The front has no fly, zipper, or button closure. The stretchable rib-knit waistband allows the pants to be pulled on, and a flat drawstring adjusts the waist fit. With the hem drawstrings loosened, the legs fall naturally to open hems. Tightening each cord gathers the corresponding hem and adjusts its fit around the ankle.

Both the main sweatshirt fabric and the waistband rib are substantial heavyweight knits. The waistband has a relatively firm tendency to return to its resting shape after stretching, so the amount of pressure felt at the waist will vary with body shape and personal preference. The garment measurements below are taken with the fabric relaxed and do not describe its dimensions while stretched on the body.

These sweatpants are supplied unwashed. Washing may cause some dimensional change, with comparatively little change across the width and a tendency toward slight shrinkage in length. The amount varies with washing, drying, and the individual garment. Please take this into account when considering your preferred fit and length, and follow the care instructions attached to the product.

Available sizes: S, M, and L.

[Approximate Size Reference]

The following is a general guide based on the tagged sizes you normally choose in other pants. These references describe usual pants labels, not measured body-waist ranges or the relaxed waist measurements of these sweatpants.

Tagged Size S: For customers who usually choose pants tagged approximately 29-30 inches.
Tagged Size M: For customers who usually choose pants tagged approximately 31-32 inches.
Tagged Size L: For customers who usually choose pants tagged approximately 33-34 inches.

The rib-knit waistband stretches during wear, and the drawstring can be tightened to adjust the fit. Because the rib is thick and has a relatively firm recovery, your preferred amount of pressure at the waist is an important consideration. Body shape, waistband position, preferred room, and the fit through the hips and thighs can also affect which size is suitable. Please use this guide together with the actual garment measurements, rather than treating it as an exact size conversion.

Our model is wearing a tagged size S. He is 5'9" (175 cm) tall, weighs 130 lbs (59 kg), and has a chest size of 36 inches (91 cm). He normally wears size 29 in jeans.

[Actual Garment Measurements]

The following measurements are taken from the garment itself, not from the wearer's body. The waist measurement is the relaxed waistband width measured flat and doubled. It is not the maximum waist size that the waistband can accommodate. Thigh and leg opening measurements are the flat widths of one leg and are not doubled.

Because a rib-knit gusset occupies the crotch area, there is no single conventional crotch-seam intersection to use as a measuring point. We use the point where the two legs begin to separate when the pants are laid flat as a shared reference point. Inseam, front rise, and thigh width are therefore listed as reference measurements. Please read the measuring methods below when comparing these figures with another pair.

Before choosing your size, please measure a similar pair of sweatpants that fits you well and compare its measurements with those listed above. A pair with a similarly substantial, stretchable waistband will provide a more useful comparison than pants with a rigid waistband. Please consider the seat, thigh, rise, and leg measurements as well as the waist, and use the product-specific measuring methods below.

[How We Measure the Actual Garment]

The pants are laid flat and measured by hand with a measuring tape, without stretching the knit fabric. For the inseam, front rise, and thigh measurements, the shared reference point is the point where the left and right legs begin to separate when the garment is laid flat. This is a practical measuring reference for the gusseted construction, not a conventional crotch-seam intersection.

Waist: With the rib-knit waistband resting naturally and unstretched, measure straight across its top edge from side to side, then double that measurement. The resulting figure represents the relaxed circumference of the garment's waistband. Although this figure may appear small compared with your usual pants size, the rib stretches to follow the body during wear. It does not indicate the maximum wearable waist measurement. The heavyweight rib has a relatively firm recovery, and comfort will depend partly on your preference for waistband pressure.

Inseam (Reference): Measure from the shared reference point described above to the hem, following the inside edge of one leg.

Front Rise (Reference): Lay the pants flat with the front facing up. Measure from the center of the top edge of the front waistband down to the shared reference point, following the center of the front body.

Thigh Width (Reference): At a point approximately 3cm (1.2") below the shared reference point, measure straight across one leg from its outside edge to its inside edge. This is a flat width, not a circumference.

Leg Opening: Fully loosen the hem drawstring and lay the opening flat. Measure straight across the bottom of one leg from edge to edge. This figure is the width of the open, ungathered hem.

Front rise and inseam follow different measuring paths from the full outside length of the pants, so adding the two figures may not give the overall length. With this gusseted design, the placement of the shared reference point can also affect the reference measurements.

Please allow for slight differences caused by the stretchable knit, how the garment is laid out, measuring position, reference-point placement, and variation between individual pairs. Fit will also depend on where you wear the waistband, the room you prefer through the seat and thighs, and dimensional changes after washing. The approximate size guide and the relaxed garment measurements should be considered together.

Made in Japan.
Brand new, in unused condition.
- All measurements are taken manually with the garment laid flat.
- Slight measurement differences may occur between individual garments and measuring methods.
- Actual color may differ slightly from the photographs due to lighting and screen settings.

Classic American Athletic Wear-Inspired Construction
The TMC2665 draws on the practical details of classic American athletic wear and vintage sweatpants. Its design brings together heavyweight cotton sweatshirt fleece, a substantial rib-knit waistband, a rib-knit crotch gusset, and drawstrings at both the waist and hems.

The vintage-inspired character is expressed through the garment's construction as well as its fabric. The absence of outside leg seams leaves the outer leg surface uninterrupted, while the inserted crotch panel, inset front pocket openings, and reinforced cord openings provide the functional details of the design. These features give the pants a classic athletic appearance suited to everyday casual wear.

Regular Straight Silhouette with a Gentle Taper
The cut provides moderate room through the seat and thighs, followed by a very gentle narrowing toward the hems. The overall shape remains regular and straight in appearance, with balanced proportions through the upper and lower legs.

With the hem drawstrings fully loosened, the open bottoms allow the fabric to fall naturally. Tightening the cords gathers the hems and brings the openings closer around the ankles. This adjustment changes the shape at the bottom of each leg while retaining the room through the seat and thighs.

Heavyweight 100% Cotton Sweatshirt Fleece
The main fabric is heavyweight sweatshirt fleece made from 100% cotton. It has substantial thickness and weight, with enough firmness and body to give the pants a defined shape. The cotton also provides natural suppleness, so the fabric combines a substantial feel with flexibility during wear.

The face and reverse have distinct textures. The outer surface shows the fine color variation of the black heather knit, while the reverse is brushed to create a soft, raised surface against the skin. The thickness of the fabric and its brushed interior work together to provide warmth.

Black Heather Surface and Brushed Interior
The color is 031 Black Heather. Fine white yarns are visible throughout the predominantly black knitted surface, producing the small variations in light and dark associated with a heathered or marled appearance. This gives the fabric visual depth beyond a uniform solid color.

Brushing raises fibers on the reverse of the fabric, giving the inside a soft, gently fuzzy texture. The amount and appearance of the raised fibers may vary slightly between different areas of the garment.

With wear, friction, and washing, some of these fibers may lie flatter or become compressed, particularly in areas that receive repeated contact. This is a natural change in brushed sweatshirt fabric. Slight differences in heather pattern, surface fuzz, and interior brushing may also be visible between individual pairs.

Unwashed Finish and Dimensional Changes
These sweatpants have not been washed during production. In their new condition, the heavyweight knit retains its initial thickness, firmness, and body.

As the knit contracts during washing, the stitches draw closer together and the fabric can develop a more compact feel. Continued wear and washing also bring out the suppleness of the cotton, allowing the garment to gradually conform to the wearer while retaining some of its substantial body.

This change in the knit may be accompanied by slight changes in garment dimensions. Changes across the width tend to be comparatively small, while lengthwise measurements may show some shrinkage. The amount depends on washing method, drying conditions, and the individual garment; it should not be treated as a fixed shrinkage allowance.

Hand wash gently according to the attached care label, reshape the garment, and allow it to dry naturally in the shade. Avoid warm or hot water and machine drying, as heat can increase contraction of the cotton and knitted structure, resulting in greater dimensional change or distortion.

Leg Construction without Outside Seams
The legs are constructed without outseams, meaning there are no seams running down the outside of either leg. The leg seams are positioned along the inner legs. This arrangement preserves an uninterrupted fabric surface down the outside of the pants and forms part of their classic sweatpants construction.

Rib-Knit Crotch Gusset
A stretchable rib-knit gusset is inserted into the crotch area between the legs. This separate panel adds room and flexibility where the two legs meet, helping the garment accommodate movements such as spreading or bending the legs and sitting down.

The gusset provides stretch within the crotch area itself. Its construction also means that the pants do not have the single, clearly defined crotch-seam intersection commonly used to measure conventional pants. For this reason, the inseam, front rise, and thigh dimensions in the size guide use a shared practical reference point and are listed as reference measurements.

Substantial Rib-Knit Waistband with a Flat Drawstring
The waist is finished with a broad rib-knit waistband. The rib stretches to follow the waist and has a relatively firm tendency to return to its original shape when released. Both the waistband and the main sweatshirt fabric have a substantial heavyweight feel.

A flat drawstring runs inside the waistband. Tightening and tying the cord allows the waist fit to be adjusted in addition to the stretch provided by the rib. The cord exits are reinforced with buttonhole-style stitching, which helps limit fraying and stretching around the openings during adjustment and use.

Because the waistband is measured without stretching the rib, its listed relaxed circumference is smaller than its dimensions during wear. The firmness of the rib should also be considered when choosing a size, particularly if you prefer less pressure around the waist.

Pull-On Design without a Fly
The front has no zipper, button fastening, or fly opening. The pants use a pull-on construction, with the stretchable rib-knit waistband accommodating dressing and the drawstring providing fit adjustment once the pants are on.

Vertical Single-Welt Front Pockets
A hand pocket is positioned on each side of the front. Each pocket has a vertically arranged slit opening finished with a single welt, creating a defined entry set into the body of the pants.

The pocket bags are made from brushed sweatshirt fabric similar to the main body fabric. This gives the pocket interiors a soft, substantial feel consistent with the heavyweight construction of the garment.

Right Rear Patch Pocket
An additional patch pocket is positioned on the right side of the seat. It opens at the top and is applied to the outside of the garment. Together with the two front hand pockets, it completes the three-pocket layout.

Open Hems with Individual Flat Drawstrings
The leg openings have an open-bottom construction without rib-knit cuffs or elastic. A separate flat drawstring runs inside each hem, allowing the left and right openings to be adjusted individually.

When the cords are loosened, the hems remain open and ungathered. Tightening a cord draws the fabric into gathers, reducing the opening and adjusting the fit around the ankle. The cord exits are reinforced with buttonhole-style stitching, matching the reinforcement used at the waistband.

Military-Inspired Specification Label
A military-inspired specification label is sewn onto the left rear hip. The cloth label is printed with a specification number, type and class designations, the "TOYS McCOY & Co." brand name, "U.S. PROPERTY" lettering, a size marking, and an inspector field. Stencil-style size lettering completes the design, adding a detail reminiscent of classic military athletic wear.

Made in Japan
These sweatpants are made in Japan, combining heavyweight black heather cotton fleece with a rib-knit waistband, a flexible crotch gusset, legs without outside seams, three practical pockets, and adjustable drawstrings at the waist and hems.

Their substantial fabric and balanced regular straight silhouette suit both relaxed wear and everyday casual dressing. They can be paired with a sweatshirt or T-shirt, as well as a denim jacket, work jacket, or flight jacket, bringing classic athletic details into a range of casual outfits.

Care Instructions
Hand wash gently.
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Iron on a low setting with a pressing cloth placed between the iron and the garment.
Do not dry clean.
Do not tumble dry.
Avoid strong machine spin-drying. Reshape the garment and allow it to air-dry naturally in the shade.
Before washing, loosely tie the waistband and hem drawstrings. Using a laundry mesh bag is recommended.
The cotton knit may shrink slightly depending on washing and drying methods.
After washing, reshape the pants and dry them in a well-ventilated shaded area, without leaving the drawstrings pulled tight.
The brushed fibers on the inside may gradually flatten or become compressed in places through wear, friction, and washing.

Because these sweatpants are made from unwashed 100% cotton, slight dimensional changes may occur during the first wash and subsequent washes. Avoid warm or hot water and tumble drying, which may increase shrinkage. After washing, reshape the garment and allow it to dry naturally away from direct sunlight.

product.title: TOYS McCOY Men's MA-1 Flight Jacket, ALBERT TURNER MIL-J-8279A Reproduction, Nylon Twill Shell, Wool Pile Interlining, Made in Japan (TMJ2640, Sage)
product.body_html:
TOYS McCOY Men's MA-1 Flight Jacket, ALBERT TURNER MIL-J-8279A Reproduction, Nylon Twill Shell, Wool Pile Interlining, Made in Japan (TMJ2640, Sage)

TOYS McCOY

This men's Type MA-1 flight jacket is made in Japan by TOYS McCOY. The design reproduces a 1950s U.S. Air Force jacket manufactured by ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. to the MIL-J-8279A specification, focusing on the early configuration with a square-topped internal wind flap. Its construction combines a gray-toned Sage nylon twill shell, a full nylon lining, wool pile interlining on a cotton base fabric, and wool rib-knit trim at the collar, cuffs, and waistband. A nylon oxygen-mask hose tab, snap-fastened ICS communication-cord loops, flapless waist pockets, a zippered sleeve utility pocket, and U.S. Air Force markings reproduce the equipment-related details and appearance of the early MA-1. The substantial interlining adds warmth and volume through the body and sleeves, while the short body length and rib-knit waistband create the rounded silhouette associated with this classic flight jacket. Together, these materials and structural details bring the character of the original military garment into a reproduction suited to contemporary casual wear.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

This jacket has a classic MA-1 fit, with room through the chest and body and a comparatively short body length. The generous body width is drawn in at the waist by the rib-knit waistband, creating a rounded upper-body silhouette with a defined lower edge. The insulating interlining between the shell and lining also gives the body and sleeves more thickness and volume than an L-2-series light-zone flight jacket without an insulating interlining.

The thickness of the interlining affects the space available inside the jacket, so it may fit differently from a thinner jacket with the same flat chest-width measurement. The thickness of the clothing worn underneath, your body type, and your preferred fit will also affect how it feels when worn. Before selecting a size, please measure a similar flight jacket that fits you well, preferably one with comparable thickness and construction, and compare its chest width, body length, center-back sleeve length, sleeve length from the shoulder seam, and shoulder width with the measurements below.

Our model wears Tagged Size M. He is 175 cm / approximately 5'9" tall, weighs 59 kg / approximately 130 lbs, and has a 91 cm / approximately 36" chest. For reference, he normally wears a US/EU size S/36.

The following measurements show the garment itself, not your body measurements. Width is the flat measurement across the garment and represents half of the garment's chest circumference, not the full circumference or the wearer's chest size.

[How We Measure the Actual Garment]

- All measurements are taken by hand with the garment laid flat, using a measuring tape.

1950s ALBERT TURNER MIL-J-8279A Reproduction
This model reproduces an early Type MA-1 flight jacket made for the U.S. Air Force by ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. under the MIL-J-8279A specification. The A specification was the first revision of the original MA-1 specification, and this reproduction specifically follows the configuration with a square upper end on the internal wind flap.

The reproduction brings together the gray-toned Sage Green shell, wool pile interlining, square-topped wind flap, nylon oxygen-mask hose tab, snap-fastened communication-cord loops, flapless waist pockets, left-sleeve utility pocket, and Air Force markings. These details identify the particular early configuration being reproduced and connect its appearance to the practical equipment requirements of the original jacket.

MA-1 Development and Specification Revisions
The Type MA-1 emerged in the 1950s from the development of the Type B-15 flight-jacket series and remained in use among U.S. military aviation personnel and ground crews through successive specification revisions. The original MIL-J-8279 specification was followed by MIL-J-8279A, MIL-J-8279B, MIL-J-8279C, MIL-J-8279D, MIL-J-8279E, MIL-J-8279F, and MIL-J-8279G, with the jacket's construction changing as flight conditions, equipment, and operational requirements evolved.

Differences between specifications include the shape of the internal wind flap, equipment tabs and cord loops, lining arrangements, pocket construction, and provisions for reversible wear. Jackets with a similar overall appearance can therefore differ in their exterior details, equipment attachment points, and internal construction according to their production period, specification, and contractor. This model reproduces the early arrangement with a square-topped wind flap and equipment-related tabs and loops.

The low rib-knit collar also reflects the relationship between flight clothing and aviation equipment. Modified examples of the B-15 series replaced the large mouton collar with a knitted collar to accommodate changing equipment. The MA-1 likewise uses a low knit collar that helps reduce interference around helmets and other gear.

High-Density 100% Nylon Twill Shell in Gray-Toned Sage Green
The shell is made from 100% nylon twill woven at a high density. The closely woven fabric has a smooth, compact surface and a substantial hand, combining noticeable thickness with the flexibility needed to bend and move with the garment.

The fabric develops a restrained sheen as the direction of the light and the viewing angle change. These shifting highlights and shadows give definition to the folds and rounded volume of the jacket without obscuring the underlying weave. The Sage Green color has a gray cast, giving the shell its muted, subdued appearance.

Full 100% Nylon Lining Through the Body and Sleeves
The jacket is fully lined with 100% nylon fabric through both the body and sleeves. This smooth inner surface sits between the wearer's clothing and the insulating interlining enclosed within the jacket.

The smooth nylon reduces friction against the layers worn underneath, helping the jacket slide on and off and limiting catching as the arms move. The lining therefore contributes to ease of wear while covering the insulation throughout the body and sleeves.

100% Wool Pile Interlining on a 100% Cotton Base Fabric
An insulating pile interlining is enclosed between the nylon shell and nylon lining. Its pile is made from 100% wool, while the supporting base fabric is 100% cotton. These percentages refer to the two components separately: the wool forms the raised pile, and the cotton forms the fabric that supports it.

The interlining extends through the body and sleeves. Air held within the wool pile contributes to an insulating layer between the outer shell and the smooth inner lining, helping the jacket retain warmth.

The physical depth of the pile also gives the garment thickness and volume. This internal structure supports the rounded shape of the body and sleeves, making the interlining part of both the jacket's thermal construction and its characteristic MA-1 silhouette.

Front Zipper with T.McCOY-Marked Slider and Leather Pull Tab
The front closes with a zipper fitted with a metal slider marked "T.McCOY" and a loop-shaped metal pull. A leather tab is attached to the metal pull, extending the area available to grip when opening or closing the jacket.

The leather provides a flexible handle that can be held between the fingers, making the pull easier to grasp and helping with operation of the front zipper. The metal slider, loop-shaped pull, and leather extension form distinct components of the closure.

Square-Topped Internal Wind Flap with Zigzag Stitching
A vertical wind flap, also called a storm flap, runs behind the front zipper on the wearer's right front panel. Positioned inside the closure, it provides a backing layer behind the zipper and helps reduce drafts entering through the front opening.

The upper end of the flap is square, reproducing the shape used in the early MA-1 configuration on which this jacket is based. This outline is a specific detail of the design source, alongside the equipment tabs and flapless waist pockets.

Zigzag stitching secures the interlining inside the flap. The stitching helps hold the insulating material in position and reduces its tendency to shift or gather within the flap, while also creating the visible zigzag pattern on its surface.

Flapless, Snap-Fastened Single-Welt Waist Pockets
The front has one waist pocket on each side, with the openings set at an angle. Each opening is finished with a single welt and can be secured with a snap fastener. There is no separate exterior flap covering the pocket entrance.

This arrangement preserves the flapless waist-pocket construction of the early MA-1 being reproduced. The angled openings form a clearly defined detail on the lower front, while the snaps allow the entrances to be fastened closed. The pocket bags are made from brushed double-face fabric, giving the pocket interiors a different texture from the smooth nylon shell and body lining.

Two Interior Pockets with Cotton Drill Pocket Bags
There is one interior pocket on each front panel. Both have vertically oriented openings that can be closed with snap fasteners, providing storage inside the jacket as well as at the exterior waist.

Cotton drill is used for the interior pocket bags. These bags form the storage compartments behind the pocket openings and are separate from the nylon lining that covers the body and sleeves. Their material also differs from the brushed double-face fabric used for the exterior waist-pocket bags.

Left-Sleeve Utility Pocket with TALON Zipper and Four Pen Slots
A zippered utility pocket is positioned on the left upper sleeve. Often called a cigarette pocket, this is a characteristic detail of U.S. military nylon flight jackets. The main compartment closes with a TALON zipper, whose metal pull is fitted with a leather tab to make it easier to grasp.

The outside of the pocket also incorporates four individual pen slots. These narrow compartments separate the pens from one another and from the main zippered storage area, combining two types of storage within the sleeve-pocket assembly.

U.S. Air Force Marking Printed on the Left Sleeve
Above the utility pocket, the left sleeve carries a U.S. Air Force wing-and-star emblem together with the wording "U.S. AIR FORCE." The design is printed directly onto the nylon shell, so the marking sits on the garment fabric rather than on a separately attached patch.

Nylon Oxygen-Mask Hose Tab at the Left Chest
A nylon oxygen-mask hose tab is attached vertically beside the front zipper on the wearer's left chest. Its color is similar to that of the shell, allowing the equipment detail to blend into the Sage Green front panel while remaining visible through its shape and placement.

On the original jacket, this tab provided a point for clipping an oxygen-mask hose in place. The reproduction retains the structure of this equipment attachment detail as part of its early MA-1 configuration.

Snap-Fastened ICS Communication-Cord Loops
The jacket has snap-fastened ICS communication-cord loops at both sides of the body. The snap closures allow each loop to be opened and fastened around a cord, reflecting the practical construction of the original equipment detail.

On the original design, these loops were used to retain wiring associated with headsets, microphones, and the aircraft's communication system. Their presence complements the oxygen-mask hose tab and reproduces the equipment-related features of this early specification.

100% Wool Rib-Knit Trim and Low Knit Collar
The collar, cuffs, and waistband are all made from 100% wool rib knit. The knitted structure provides flexibility and stretch at the jacket's neck, wrist, and waist openings, allowing these areas to follow the body while the nylon shell retains its fuller shape.

At the neckline, the low collar follows the neck without the height or bulk of a large mouton collar. Its flexible construction helps accommodate neck and shoulder movement, while the closer fit around the opening helps reduce the entry of wind.

Stepped Rib-Knit Cuffs with Two Rib Textures
The cuffs use a stepped rib-knit construction in which the rib pattern changes partway along the cuff. The section adjoining the nylon sleeve has wider ribs, while the section toward the wrist opening has finer ribs. This creates a visible transition in the knitted texture within each cuff.

The stretch of the wool knit allows the cuffs to sit comfortably around the wrists and helps limit drafts entering through the sleeve openings. Drawing the full nylon sleeves inward at the wrists also helps hold the sleeve ends in position and gives the sleeves their rounded volume above the cuffs.

Rib-Knit Waistband and Rounded MA-1 Silhouette
The bottom of the jacket is finished with a wool rib-knit waistband. Its stretch draws the comparatively roomy body inward at the waist, giving the lower edge a closer fit than the chest and upper body.

The resulting shape comes from the combination of a short body, room through the chest, the volume of the internal insulation, and the narrowing effect of the waistband. These elements work together to create the rounded, waist-length silhouette associated with the MA-1 flight jacket.

Reproduction ALBERT TURNER Contractor Label
A reproduction ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. contractor label is sewn inside the back neckline. Its wording includes "JACKET, FLYING, MAN'S, INTERMEDIATE," "TYPE MA-1," "SPEC. MIL-J-8279A," "ORDER NO. AF 33(602)-8077," and "ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC."

These markings reproduce the garment designation, type, specification number, order number, and contractor identification found on the military label being recreated. The label records the historical design source represented by this TOYS McCOY reproduction.

White U.S. Air Force Marking Inside the Back Neckline
Below the contractor label, a U.S. Air Force wing-and-star emblem and the words "U.S. AIR FORCE" are printed in white directly onto the lining. This places a second Air Force marking inside the jacket, in addition to the marking on the left sleeve.

The interior print is normally hidden when the jacket is worn. Reproducing it beneath the label carries the early MA-1 detailing into the back-neck lining as well as the exterior shell.

Made in Japan
TOYS McCOY model TMJ2640 is made in Japan as a reproduction of the ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. MIL-J-8279A configuration. Its gray-toned Sage Green nylon twill, wool pile interlining, and wool rib-knit trim establish the material character and rounded shape of the jacket.

The square-topped wind flap, flapless waist pockets, sleeve utility pocket, oxygen-mask hose tab, communication-cord loops, contractor label, and Air Force markings complete the early specification being recreated. Together, the fabric, insulation, and construction details preserve the practical character of the original design in a flight jacket for everyday casual wear.

Care Instructions
Do not wash at home.
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Do not tumble dry.
Do not iron.
Do not dry clean.
Do not professionally wet clean.
Consult a specialist cleaner for advice on appropriate care.

Always follow the care instructions attached to the actual product. When consulting a specialist, show them the care label so they can assess an appropriate method for this jacket.

Additional Precautions for Care and Handling

Protecting the Jacket’s Shape
Water and heat can cause wool insulation, rib-knit components, and leather details to shrink or become distorted, affecting the jacket’s overall shape. Do not soak, wash, or tumble dry this jacket.

Protecting the Air Force Marking
Dry-cleaning solvents may fade or completely remove heat-transfer Air Force markings. Do not dry clean this jacket.

Localized Stain Treatment
For localized stains, consult a specialist about whether gentle wiping with a cloth dampened with a diluted mild, pH-neutral detergent is appropriate. Spot treatment may cause uneven coloration, so any proposed method should first be tested in an inconspicuous area. Always follow the jacket’s actual care label.

Avoid Artificial Distressing
Do not deliberately soil or distress the jacket to create a worn appearance, as this may damage the fabric or components.

This men's long-sleeve zip-up hoodie is made in Japan by Barns Outfitters as part of its COZUN series. Drawing on the practical construction of classic American athletic wear and vintage sweatshirts, the design brings together carefully developed fabric, knitting, stitching, and functional garment details. Its medium-weight 100% cotton sweatshirt fabric is knitted on COZUN small-diameter knitting machines. These machines are modified versions of older sinker knitting machines that were used during the transition from traditional loopwheel machines to high-speed sinker knitting machines. The name COZUN comes from the Japanese term for these small-diameter machines. By knitting slowly while limiting tension on the yarn and the developing fabric, this process produces a soft, supple hand together with moderate firmness and body. This balance gives the fabric a comfortable, yielding feel while providing enough structure to support the hoodie's outline. The reverse is brushed to create a soft, full interior, with the raised cotton fibers holding air and contributing to warmth. A two-way front zipper, double-layer hood, rib-knit underarm gussets, extended cuffs and waistband, and visible flatseam stitching give the plain design its distinctive character. The one-wash finish further softens the initial feel while preserving the fabric's underlying body. A slightly slim silhouette keeps excess volume to a minimum, allowing the hoodie to work as an everyday outer layer or beneath a jacket. Together, the distinctive COZUN fabric and practical construction details bring the character of vintage athletic clothing into contemporary casual wear.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

The hoodie has a slightly slim, streamlined fit, with a body that does not flare outward and relatively close-cut armholes. It follows the body naturally while retaining moderate ease, limiting excess fabric through the torso and sleeves. The body length is moderate rather than especially cropped, giving it proportions that work with both casual outfits and a cleaner, more put-together style.

Set-in sleeves create a defined shoulder line. The deep rib-knit waistband draws the lower body inward only gently, allowing the fabric to fall naturally from the torso to the hem without a strongly cinched waist. Extended rib-knit cuffs provide a comfortable fit around the wrists. The relatively restrained volume also makes the hoodie suitable for layering under a jacket or coat.

Fit will vary with your body type, the thickness of the clothing worn underneath, and your preferred amount of ease. Classic American Athletic-Wear Construction
The design takes its starting point from the practical construction of classic American athletic wear and vintage sweatshirts. The emphasis is on the relationship between the fabric, garment panels, rib-knit components, and stitching. The plain exterior allows the knitted texture, panel junctions, and functional details to remain visible without relying on added decoration.

The two-way zipper provides adjustable front coverage, while the double-layer hood, underarm gussets, and extended rib-knit finishes give each opening and junction a specific role. These details are combined with a relatively streamlined silhouette, preserving the familiar character of a traditional sweatshirt hoodie in proportions suited to everyday casual wear.

COZUN Small-Diameter Knitting
The sweatshirt fabric is knitted on a COZUN small-diameter knitting machine. The name COZUN comes from the Japanese term for this type of small-diameter machine. Its construction is based on a modified older sinker knitting machine of the type used during the transition from loopwheel machines to modern high-speed sinker knitting equipment.

The fabric is knitted slowly while limiting tension on the yarn and the developing knit. This process produces a soft hand together with moderate firmness and body. The softness allows the material to settle comfortably against the wearer, while its underlying structure helps support the outline of the hoodie.

Medium-Weight 100% Cotton Sweatshirt Fabric with 30/7 Yarn Construction
The fabric is a medium-weight sweatshirt knit made from 100% cotton. It has a moderate thickness and a soft feel, balancing substance with flexibility. The construction uses No. 30 cotton yarn on the face and thicker No. 7 cotton yarn on the reverse. The relatively fine face yarn forms the more finely textured outer surface, while the thicker backing yarn contributes fullness to the interior.

Fine columns of knit stitches run vertically along the face. Slight variations in the knitted surface and the natural fuzz of the cotton give the fabric a subtle, irregular texture reminiscent of vintage sweatshirts. This surface character comes from the yarn and knitting rather than an added printed pattern.

Soft Brushed Interior
The reverse of the sweatshirt fabric is brushed to raise the cotton fibers into a soft, full surface. This gives the inside a cushioned feel against the body and distinguishes it from an unbrushed sweatshirt knit.

The raised fibers create small spaces that hold air within the brushed surface, contributing to warmth. The resulting fabric combines a relatively fine outer face with a fuller interior, maintaining the moderate overall thickness of a medium-weight sweatshirt.

One-Wash Finish
The hoodie is washed once during finishing. This initial wash softens the fabric's crispness while retaining moderate body, giving it a more settled feel from the first wear. Compared with an unwashed garment, it is less prone to substantial initial shrinkage because it has already undergone a wash before sale.

The finish does not eliminate the possibility of further dimensional change. As a 100% cotton knitted garment, it may still shrink slightly or change in size depending on subsequent washing and drying conditions and differences between individual garments. With continued wear and washing, the fabric gradually settles further and develops a more naturally worn-in texture.

Two-Way Front Zipper
The front uses a two-way zipper with two sliders. Once the zipper is fastened, the upper slider allows the opening at the chest and neckline to be adjusted, while the lower slider allows the front to open upward from the hem.

Opening the lower section slightly when seated gives the fabric more room around the abdomen and hips. This can reduce tightness and pulling in the lower body, improving comfort and limiting strain on the fabric where it would otherwise be drawn taut.

The lower opening also allows part of an underlying shirt to show while the upper section remains closed. The two sliders therefore provide control over both the way the hoodie sits on the body and the appearance of the front opening.

Double-Layer Hood with a Center Seam and No Drawcord
The hood uses two layers of the same sweatshirt fabric as the body. The layers are arranged so that the fabric's face is visible on both the outside and the inside of the hood. The brushed reverse surfaces sit between the layers, leaving the finer knitted face exposed on either side.

The left and right hood sections are joined along a vertical center seam to create a shaped, three-dimensional form. The combined thickness of the two layers and the center seam help support the hood's outline, allowing it to stand naturally around the back of the neck and retain a defined shape.

The opening is made without a drawcord. This keeps the front edge visually simple, allowing the doubled fabric and shaped construction to define the hood's appearance.

Set-In Sleeves with One-Piece Sleeve Bodies
The long sleeves use a set-in construction, with each sleeve cap sewn into the corresponding armhole in the body. The resulting shoulder and armhole seams define the transition between the torso and sleeve, giving the upper body a neat outline.

Each main sleeve section is made from a single fabric panel whose edges are joined along the underside of the arm to form a tube. This lengthwise underarm seam closes the sleeve body, while the cuff is attached as a separate rib-knit component at the wrist.

Stretch Rib-Knit Underarm Gussets
A separate rib-knit gusset is inserted at each underarm where the sleeve joins the body. The gusset is sewn to the surrounding panels, creating a section of more flexible fabric at the sleeve attachment.

As the arms are raised or extended forward, the rib knit stretches with the movement. This helps ease pulling around the base of the sleeve and supplements freedom of movement through the armhole. Its role is particularly useful in a hoodie with relatively close-cut armholes, where a flexible junction helps accommodate movement without adding broad overall volume.

Extended Double-Layer Rib-Knit Cuffs
The cuffs use rib knit produced separately from the main sweatshirt fabric. Each cuff is folded back on itself to form a double layer, then sewn to the end of the sleeve. The folded construction gives the wrist opening a defined edge, while the rib knit provides stretch.

The knit becomes finer toward the cuff edge from the seam where the cuff meets the sleeve. Together with the elasticity of the rib structure, this helps the cuff conform comfortably around the wrist.

The cuffs are longer than those commonly found on standard sweatshirts, covering a greater area around the wrists. Their close, flexible fit helps limit the entry of cold air through the sleeve openings, while their extended proportions contribute to the hoodie's vintage athletic-wear appearance.

Deep Double-Layer Rib-Knit Waistband
The lower body is finished with a comparatively deep rib-knit waistband. As with the cuffs, the rib knit is folded into a double layer and sewn to the main sweatshirt body, creating a substantial but flexible lower edge.

The waistband has greater stretch than the main fabric, allowing it to follow the waist and help the hem sit securely. Its inward pull is restrained, so it does not strongly cinch the lower body. Instead, the silhouette falls naturally from the torso toward the hem, preserving the hoodie's relatively clean, straight-looking lower profile.

Split Kangaroo-Style Patch Pockets
Two kangaroo-style patch pockets sit at the lower front, one on each side of the zipper. Each pocket is made from a separate piece of the same sweatshirt fabric, laid over and stitched to the outside of the body. The space between the pocket panel and the body forms the storage compartment.

The left and right pockets are separate compartments. Each has an angled opening at its outer side, positioned to allow the hand to enter naturally from the side. In addition to holding small items, the pockets can be used as hand warmers.

The edges of the openings are turned back and secured with stitching. This reinforces the pocket mouths where repeated hand entry places stress on the fabric. The openings are relatively broad, so please take care that items do not fall out.

The inner edges follow the line of the front zipper, and the lower edges extend to the junction between the body and the rib-knit waistband. Their symmetrical placement and slanted openings create the recognizable front arrangement associated with classic athletic hoodies.

Flatseamer Construction for Low-Profile Seams
The main components are joined with flatlock seams sewn on a flatseamer. Compared with constructions that leave raised seam allowances on the inside, this method keeps the junctions relatively flat and limits abrupt changes in thickness where the fabric sections meet.

Controlling these junctions helps reduce bulky ridges against the body at sewn areas such as the sides, shoulders, armholes, underarm gussets, sleeve undersides, cuffs, pockets, and waistband. The construction allows the sweatshirt to retain its fabric thickness while keeping the seams less prominent against the wearer.

Visible Stitching That Outlines the Garment Structure
The flatseam stitching also forms part of the exterior design. Stitch lines remain visible along the component junctions, outlining the changes between the body panels, sleeves, gussets, rib-knit sections, and pockets.

On the plain design, these lines provide a restrained visual accent while making the construction easier to see. The appearance comes from the stitching used to assemble the garment, linking its decorative effect directly to the structure of the hoodie.

Made in Japan
This COZUN zip-up hoodie is made in Japan. Its softly textured cotton fabric combines moderate thickness with enough body to support the garment, while the double-layer hood, flexible underarm gussets, extended rib-knit finishes, and flat seams give each section a distinct structural role.

The adjustable two-way zipper and relatively streamlined fit make it practical as an everyday outer layer or beneath a jacket or coat. With minimal added decoration, its character comes from the knitting, stitching, and construction of the individual parts.

Care Instructions
Machine wash on a very gentle cycle at a maximum water temperature of 40°C (104°F).
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Do not tumble dry.
Hang to dry in the shade.
Iron on a low setting with a pressing cloth.
Do not dry clean.
Professional wet cleaning using a very gentle process is permitted.
